title: Roots & Irrational Numbers
subtitle: Square Roots, Cube Roots & Estimates
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b Roots. Square roots only of the perfect squares 4-100 and cube roots only of 1, 8, 27, 64 (cube roots are written in words, 'Cube root of 27'); a side or edge comes from an area or volume of that kind. An irrational number is an unsimplified √n (n 2-99, not a perfect square) or π; no radical is simplified, added or multiplied. Repeating decimals have 1 or 2 repeating digits (0.777..., 0.1818..., or one digit after a non-repeating one: 0.1666...) and a fraction in simplest form with numerator and denominator 1-12 (ninths, elevenths, sixths); terminating decimals convert to fractions with denominator 2-10. The 10x − x step shows x with 1 or 2 repeating digits and an answer 1-90. Estimates name the whole numbers around √n (n 2-99) or the nearest whole number (the decimal part of √n is under 0.3 or over 0.7) or k.5 for √(k(k+1)) with k 2-9. Any two values compared differ by at least 0.3; an ordering has 3 values. Wrong choices: whatever a misreading gives, up to 999.

HALVED.student: A square root is not half. Ask: what times itself makes the number?
HALVED.teacher: Divides by 2 instead of taking the root (√49 = 24.5).

DOUBLED.student: Not double. √49 asks what number times itself makes 49.
DOUBLED.teacher: Doubles the root instead of squaring or rooting (√49 = 14).

NOT_ROOTED.student: That is the number itself. The root times itself makes that number.
NOT_ROOTED.teacher: Gives the number back without taking the root.

THIRD_FOR_CUBE.student: A cube root is not dividing by 3. Find a number used 3 times in a product.
THIRD_FOR_CUBE.teacher: Divides by 3 for a cube root (cube root of 27 = 9).

TRIPLED.student: A cube root is not times 3. 3 × 3 × 3 makes 27, so the root is 3.
TRIPLED.teacher: Multiplies the root by 3 instead of cubing or rooting.

SQUARE_ROOT_FOR_CUBE.student: That is the square root. A cube root uses the number three times.
SQUARE_ROOT_FOR_CUBE.teacher: Takes the square root where a cube root was asked (cube root of 64 = 8).

POSITIVE_ONLY.student: Both signs square to the same number. Check the sign the question asks for.
POSITIVE_ONLY.teacher: Ignores the negative solution, or ignores the sign condition.

AREA_OVER_4.student: Side × side = area. Dividing by 4 would find a side only for a perimeter.
AREA_OVER_4.teacher: Divides the area by 4 (perimeter thinking) instead of taking the root.

PERIMETER_FOR_SIDE.student: That is the perimeter. The side is the root of the area.
PERIMETER_FOR_SIDE.teacher: Gives 4 × side (perimeter) where the side was asked.

ROOT_IS_IRRATIONAL.student: A root sign does not make it irrational. √36 = 6 is a whole number.
ROOT_IS_IRRATIONAL.teacher: Calls every square root irrational, even of a perfect square.

ROOT_IS_RATIONAL.student: √7 is not a whole number or a fraction. It never ends or repeats.
ROOT_IS_RATIONAL.teacher: Thinks the root of a non-square is rational.

REPEAT_IS_IRRATIONAL.student: A repeating decimal is a fraction (0.333... = 1/3), so it is rational.
REPEAT_IS_IRRATIONAL.teacher: Thinks a decimal that goes on forever must be irrational.

NONWHOLE_IS_IRRATIONAL.student: Fractions and ending decimals are rational. Irrational means no fraction fits.
NONWHOLE_IS_IRRATIONAL.teacher: Thinks any number that is not a whole number is irrational.

PI_IS_RATIONAL.student: π never ends and never repeats, so it is irrational. 3.14 is only close.

OVER_TEN.student: Repeating digits are not tenths. Use 9 for one repeating digit.

ROUNDED_UP.student: Rounding changes the value. 0.666... is exactly 6/9, not 7/10.
ROUNDED_UP.teacher: Rounds the repeating decimal up, then writes it over 10.

OVER_HUNDRED.student: Two repeating digits go over 99, not 100.
OVER_HUNDRED.teacher: Uses the digits over 100 for a repeating decimal.

NINTHS_ONLY.student: Two repeating digits go over 99. That reduces to elevenths.
NINTHS_ONLY.teacher: Treats a two-digit repeat like a one-digit repeat (ninths).

NINE_FOR_TERMINATING.student: 9s are for repeating decimals. An ending decimal uses 10, 100 or 1000.
NINE_FOR_TERMINATING.teacher: Uses a denominator of 9, 99 or 999 for a decimal that ends.

DIGIT_AS_DENOM.student: 0.4 means 4 tenths. The digits go on top, not on the bottom.
DIGIT_AS_DENOM.teacher: Puts the digits in the denominator (0.4 = 1/4).

PLACE_VALUE_SLIP.student: Count decimal places: 1 is tenths, 2 hundredths, 3 thousandths.
PLACE_VALUE_SLIP.teacher: Uses the wrong place value for the denominator.

TIMES_ONLY.student: That is only 10x or 100x. Subtract x so the repeating tails cancel.
TIMES_ONLY.teacher: Multiplies by 10 or 100 but forgets to subtract x.

NINES_ONLY.student: The 9 is how many x you have. The answer is the difference of the numbers.
NINES_ONLY.teacher: Gives the coefficient of x (9 or 99) instead of the difference.

TRUNCATED_REPEAT.student: Cut-off digits lose value. 4.444... − 0.444... is exactly 4.
TRUNCATED_REPEAT.teacher: Multiplies the truncated decimal (9 × 0.4) instead of subtracting.

DECIMAL_SLIP.student: Line up the decimal points. The repeating tails cancel, leaving a whole number.
DECIMAL_SLIP.teacher: Misplaces the decimal point after subtracting.

SQUARES_NOT_ROOTS.student: Those are the squares around the number. The root is between their roots.
SQUARES_NOT_ROOTS.teacher: Names the perfect squares on each side instead of their roots.

NEXT_SQUARE_DOWN.student: Square both numbers. The radicand must sit between those two squares.
NEXT_SQUARE_DOWN.teacher: Uses the pair of whole numbers one step below the correct pair.

NEXT_SQUARE_UP.student: Square both numbers. The radicand must sit between those two squares.
NEXT_SQUARE_UP.teacher: Uses the pair of whole numbers one step above the correct pair.

NEAREST_SQUARE_NOT_ROOT.student: That is the nearest square. Its root is the whole number you want.
NEAREST_SQUARE_NOT_ROOT.teacher: Gives the nearest perfect square instead of its square root.

ROUNDED_WRONG.student: Which perfect square is closer? Its root is the nearest whole number.
ROUNDED_WRONG.teacher: Picks the far whole number when rounding a root.

RADICAND_AS_VALUE.student: A root is much smaller than the number under it. Judge √50 by 7 × 7.
RADICAND_AS_VALUE.teacher: Compares the number under the root sign, not the root's value.

ROOT_ALWAYS_SMALL.student: A root is not always the smaller one. Estimate it between two whole numbers.
ROOT_ALWAYS_SMALL.teacher: Assumes any √ expression is smaller than the other number.

ORDER_REVERSED.student: Re-read which way the list should run, least to greatest or the other way.
ORDER_REVERSED.teacher: Orders the list in the opposite direction.

GIVEN_ORDER.student: The list is not in order yet. Estimate each root, then sort.
GIVEN_ORDER.teacher: Keeps the order the numbers were written in.

TIMES_FOR_POWER.student: π^2 is π times π, about 3 × 3, not 2 × π.
TIMES_FOR_POWER.teacher: Multiplies by the exponent (2 × π) instead of squaring.
